b_door.speaker: MME BÉRANGER
lines: In. Shoes off — the widow Fouchet below has ears like a priest. You are the fourth American to stand on that mat this year; two of the others are home, so the mat is lucky. Sit.
Inside, quickly. Shoes in the hand, not on the floor — Fouchet below reports creaks the way other women report crimes. Sit. The mat you stood on is lucky; do not ask about the odds.

b_rules.speaker: MME BÉRANGER
lines: The rules are three. You do not touch the shutters. You do not answer the door, not even to God. And whatever you hear on the stairs, you are a coat in that wardrobe until I say otherwise. Repeat none of this; remember all of it.

Three rules keep this floor alive. Shutters stay shut. The door answers to my hand only. And when the stairs speak, you become a coat in the wardrobe and coats do not breathe loudly. That is the whole law.

f_intro.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: Lt. Dale Freeman, 92nd. B-17s, ball turret — don't laugh, I fit. Three weeks on this floor, buddy. Three. My ankle's done healing and the wallpaper and I are out of conversation.
Freeman. Dale. 92nd Bomb Group — ball turret, and yes, I folded in there fine. Week three in this room, pal. The ankle's healed. The wallpaper has no news. I'd trade a toe for a sidewalk.

choices.text: Boyd. Tail gunner. How's the line treating you?
Three weeks safe is three weeks alive, Lieutenant.

f_line.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: Slow. Papers, papers, wait, papers. But there's a fella — Lucien — you'll meet him, he's the only one in this town who moves. Got two Poles to Spain in nine days flat, they say.
The line? A queue with prayers. Except Lucien — he'll turn up, he brings the bread. That guy MOVES. Nine days to Spain for two Polish boys, I heard. Nine.

f_safe.speaker: FREEMAN
lines: That's what she says too. You'll fit right in — the two of you can wait at each other. Me, I count days. I'm at twenty-two.
Sure, sure — alive and mummified. You and Madame will get along; waiting's her religion. I'm at day twenty-two of the novena.

b_flat.speaker: MME BÉRANGER
lines: The lieutenant confuses a corridor with a cage. Soup is at eight. The other one will come tonight with the bread — he is charming. Note that I did not say more than that.

He calls it a cage; I call it a floor nobody has died on. Soup at eight. Tonight the bread comes, and the young man who carries it is charming — and note, monsieur, that this is the entire compliment.
